hints: Focus on what type of compound ethanal is and what each of the three reagents is testing for.
Remember that acidified dichromate changes from orange to green when it oxidises an aldehyde, and alkaline iodine gives a yellow precipitate with a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group.
Recall the difference between Fehling's solution which gives a red precipitate and Tollens' reagent which gives a silver mirror.
walkthrough:
**Identify ethanal as an aldehyde**

Ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, contains the aldehyde $\text{-CHO}$ group. This means it is easily oxidised and gives positive results with the classic oxidising and carbonyl tests.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} \text{ is an aldehyde, a reducing agent}$$

**Reaction 1 with acidified dichromate**

Acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is a strong oxidiser. It oxidises the aldehyde to ethanoic acid and is itself reduced from orange $\text{Cr(VI)}$ to green $\text{Cr(III)}$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + [O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$
$$\text{orange Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} \rightarrow \text{green Cr}^{3+}$$

**Reaction 2 with alkaline iodine, the iodoform test**

Ethanal contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ group, so with alkaline $\text{I}_2(aq)$ and heat it undergoes the tri-iodoform reaction. The product is triiodomethane, $\text{CHI}_3$, seen as a pale yellow precipitate.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3(s) + \text{HCOO}^- + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Reaction 3 with Fehling's solution**

Fehling's solution contains blue $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ complex. An aldehyde reduces it on boiling to copper(I) oxide, $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$, which is a brick-red solid. The silver mirror is only formed with Tollens' reagent, not Fehling's.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + 2\text{Cu}^{2+} + 5\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^- + \text{Cu}_2\text{O}(s) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Combine the three observations**

Solution 1 is green, solid 2 is yellow, solid 3 is red. This matches green, yellow, red.

options.A: Green for solution 1 and yellow for solid 2 are correct, but silver mirror is wrong for solid 3. Silver mirror is the positive result with Tollens' reagent, not with Fehling's solution which gives red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$.
options.B: Correct. Excess ethanal reduces orange dichromate to green $\text{Cr}^{3+}$, gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate in the iodoform test, and gives red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ precipitate with Fehling's solution.
options.C: Incorrect. Orange would mean no reduction of dichromate, but aldehydes are oxidised so the colour must change to green. Red for solid 2 confuses iodoform ($\text{CHI}_3$, yellow) with Fehling's ($\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$, red), and silver mirror confuses Fehling's with Tollens'.
options.D: Red for solid 3 is correct, but orange for solution 1 and red for solid 2 are wrong. Orange means unreacted dichromate, yet ethanal is oxidised. Red solid 2 mixes up the yellow iodoform precipitate with the red Fehling's precipitate.
